cards.questionText:
Date: September 23, 2005
From: Hymills@Mills.com
To: zenap23@happy.co
Subject: Stationary Order 

This is just to (1)_____ the order placed over the telephone earlier today. As we discussed before, I would like to order the (2)_____ items: 

32 boxes of A4 paper, white, recycled
20 boxes of A4 paper, white (NOT recycled)
2 packs of A4 paper, green
2 boxes of black ball point pens (the cheapest you have in stock)
1 box of red ball point pens
15 large glue sticks, any brand

I would also like to confirm that this order will be (3)_____ to our account, as is our usual policy. Please send the (4)_____ as soon as it is ready. I need to submit it to the accounting department before the end of the week.

Thank you for your consideration,
Hayley Mills

childQuestions.transcript:
"Confirm" means to verify or officially state that something is correct. In business emails, it is very common to write to confirm an order after discussing it by phone.

  • notify = inform someone about something (wrong meaning)
  • refer = mention or direct attention to something
  • respect = admire or show consideration for someone

"The following items" is a fixed expression meaning "the items listed below."

  • below → We usually say "the items below," but after "order the ___ items," "following" sounds more natural and formal.
  • preceding = coming before (the opposite meaning)
  • under = beneath; not used in this context

"Charge something to an account" means the company will pay later through its business account instead of paying immediately.

  • asked = requested
  • bought = purchased
  • taken = received or carried away

None of these fit the phrase: "___ to our account."

An invoice is a document that shows what was purchased, the quantity, price, and amount due. Accounting departments need invoices for payment records.

  • arrangement = plan or agreement
  • notice = announcement or warning
  • papers = general documents (too vague)

Clue in the text: I need to submit it to the accounting department before the end of the week. => The accounting department usually requires an invoice.

cards.questionText:
Dear Mrs. Whitman,

I regret to inform you that your application for a government subsidized housing (1)_____ has been rejected. While we understand that you recently became unemployed, as a home owner who has more than $10,000 dollars currently (2)_____ in a bank account, you simply do not fit any of the basic criteria for a subsidized housing loan. However, as a single parent, if you are receiving no financial support from the father of your children, you may qualify for child care assistance. I suggest that you contact our office to make an appointment to discuss this further. The number to call for (3)_____ appointments is 023-445-4460. The phone line is operational between the hours of 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. Please have your social security number on hand when you call. This (4)_____ speed up the process. 

Sincerely,

Clarence Dewitt

childQuestions.transcript:
A loan is money borrowed from a bank or government that must be repaid later.

The letter explains that the applicant does not meet the requirements for a subsidized housing loan, so this is the most logical choice.

  • affirmation = a positive statement or confirmation 
  • agree = a verb, not a noun 
  • permission = authorization to do something 

Vocabulary:

  • housing loan = home loan
  • subsidized loan = a loan partly supported by the government

Deposit means to put money into a bank account.

The sentence describes money that is already in her account.

  • mortgage = a home loan 
  • transfer = move money from one account to another 
  • withdrawn = taken out of an account

A consultation is a meeting to discuss a problem or receive advice.

The office is inviting Mrs. Whitman to make an appointment to discuss possible child-care assistance.

  • denomination = a type or value of money/religious group 
  • remittance = money sent to someone 
  • talking = informal and unnatural here

The writer is talking about a future result.

If she has her Social Security number ready, it will help make the process faster.

  • helped = past tense 
  • is helping = present continuous 
  • used to help = describes a past habit 

Examples:

  • Exercising regularly will help improve your health.
  • Having the documents ready will help speed up the application process.

cards.questionText:
Over the last few months, we have received (1)_____ letters from readers, asking us where they can buy some of the items that have been on display in the background of a number of our fashion features. It almost seems that the furnishings and decorative items from those photo shoots have (2)_____ interest than the clothes themselves.

For this reason you will notice that, starting on page 78 of this month's edition, we have introduced a new feature entitled "Where can I buy...?" This new section will appear immediately after our main fashion photo feature each month. We will be listing the designers and manufacturers for just about everything you can see in each photo, and we will be giving you the numbers and websites you need to find out more. Many of these items will be made available at a (3)_____ to magazine subscribers. 

All the more reason to take out a subscription! 

Take a (4)_____ and let us know what you think.

childQuestions.transcript:
"Letters" is a countable plural noun, so we need an expression that can modify plural countable nouns.

a lot of letters = many letters

  • lots  → should be lots of letters
  • much  → used with uncountable nouns (much money, much information)
  • numbers of  → should be a number of letters

Examples;

  • We received a lot of emails.
  • There are a lot of customers today.

Arouse interest = make people interested in something.

Because the sentence contains "than the clothes themselves", a comparative form (more) is required.

  • aroused  → missing the comparison ("more")
  • made more  → we say arouse interest, not make more interest
  • provoked  → usually provokes reactions, anger, controversy, not interest in this context

The fixed expression is: "at a discount" =>  meaning at a reduced price.

  • bargain  → usually "at a bargain price"
  • major retailer  → completely different meaning
  • price off  → incorrect expression

Example:

  • Members can buy tickets at a discount.
  • The store offers a 20% discount.

This is a very common expression: take a look = have a look = examine something

  • break  → take a break (different meaning)
  • off  → impossible
  • time  → take time (different structure)

Example: 

  • Take a look at our new website.
  • Please take a look and give me your opinion.

cards.questionText:
To:         Fiona Kim

From:     Baljit Singh

Subject: Urgent Busines

Ms. Kim: 

I wish you to present yourself at my office at 9:00 a.m. tomorrow. It has been (1)_____ to my attention by various members of staff that you have not been acting in a very cooperative manner of late, and I feel we need to meet to discuss the (2)_____. I was very surprised to hear this, and although I have been ignoring it, hoping that this was a temporary matter, it has been going on long enough that I think we need to talk.

I will not go into (3)_____ in this memo, but needless to say we will be discussing three major incidents which have caused us to lose important contracts. I have not yet decided what will happen to your position at this company; it depends rather on the outcome of our meeting tomorrow and the outcome of a second meeting that I will have with both of your (4)_____ tomorrow afternoon.

childQuestions.transcript:
This is a very common business expression: bring something to someone's attention = make someone aware of something.

The sentence is in the passive voice: It has been brought to my attention...

Example: The problem was brought to my attention yesterday.

The manager is referring generally to Fiona's recent behavior and its consequences.

Situation = a set of circumstances or problems that need attention.

  • circumstance: usually used in the plural (circumstances)
  • development: means a new event or change
  • event: refers to one specific occurrence

Example: We need to discuss the situation before making a decision.

The fixed expression is: go into details = explain something thoroughly.

The manager does not want to explain everything in the memo because it will be discussed in the meeting.

  • carefully: adverb; doesn't fit after "go into"
  • in detail: We say go into detail (singular), not go into in detail
  • information: incorrect collocation

A supervisor is a person who directly oversees an employee's work.

The manager wants to hear from the people responsible for monitoring Fiona's performance.

  • foreman: mainly used in factories/construction
  • leaders: too general
  • watchers: not used in business contexts
